name: service_police_c
prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 9 police cars for a 2D top-down city game, made by repainting the cars of the first picture.

The first picture is nine finished cars in a 3×3 grid. Redraw it exactly — the same nine cars in the same places, at the same size, with the same outlines, proportions, glass, mirrors, lamps, shading and art style, straight down from above — and turn each into a police car of the town, painted like the police car in the second picture.

KEEP EVERY BODY EXACTLY AS WIDE AS IN THE FIRST PICTURE: do not widen, round out or enlarge any car — trace each outline from the first picture. Car 1 is a short boxy Soviet three-door small 4×4: flat bonnet, upright square cab, short flat roof, square tail, exactly as the first picture draws it, not an estate or a hatchback.

NOTHING ON THE ROOF. Draw no light bar, no beacon, no dome and no roof rails on any car, whatever the second picture shows: the game fits its own light bar later. Every roof is plain smooth paint, white (car 8's black, as in the first picture).

Livery:
- The whole body painted white, every panel, bonnet to boot — the two old cars, 1 and 2, a slightly yellowed white; no panel left in the first picture's colour. A thin dark blue stripe runs the length of each flank just inside the outline, and a blue edge round the bonnet like the second picture's.
- On the middle of the bonnet a police badge emblem: a dark blue shield shape with a gold-yellow outline and a small gold-yellow star in its centre, about a third of the bonnet's width. No text, letters, numbers or real crests anywhere.
- The glass dark, the lamps exactly where and as the first picture draws them, switched off: the tail lamps clean lenses in their housings, no red smeared onto the bodywork round them.
Change nothing else: not the shape, not the length or width, not the position. Car 6 (the van) keeps its van body.

Background: fully transparent outside the cars — no colour, no glow or halo, no shadow. Each car's edge ends sharply.

The cars, left to right and top to bottom: 1 a Soviet three-door small 4×4, 2 a 1980s Soviet saloon, 3 a modern hatchback, 4 a modern budget compact SUV, 5 a plain modern budget saloon, 6 a modern small panel van, 7 a modern hybrid liftback, 8 a modern compact crossover, 9 a modern compact saloon.
